item.title: #199- Rachel & Timothee: Off The Menu
item.description:
Rachel Gouk is the creator of the popular Shanghai food blog Nomfluence.  She is also the founder of Shanghai Burger Month and a consultant for F&B brands.  Timothee Becqueriaux is an accomplished mixologist and bartender, currently spearheading the cocktail program at Bar Mixato.  He is also a winner of the global Chivas Masters cocktail competition.  Today we talk about food, taste and love.  We compare dining standards between Europe and Shanghai, and debate “authenticity” versus personal memory in taste. We dissect how awards and ratings (Michelin, 50 Best, Dianping) are gamified, and float the idea of “food Tinder”.  We discuss cultural differences in communal versus individual dining, how palates evolve (bitterness, spice), favorite comfort foods, curry preferences, cooking at home, and the thin margins and pressures of running F&B.  We also talk about Rachel and Timothee’s relationship as a romantic couple and how food plays a central role keeping them together despite there differences.  This is a wild one where we go off-script and off-menu.

item.title: #198- Lee Mack: The Carrot or the Stick
item.description:

item.title: #196- Yaling Jiang: Through Chinese Eyes
item.description:
Yaling Jiang is a writer and researcher helping people understand China through real individuals, rather than through headlines or stereotypes.  Yaling is a former journalist and translator and founder of the popular newsletter Following the Yuan.  She is also the founder of the research and strategy consultancy ApertureChina.  Today, Yaling joins us to talk about what it really means to explain China to the outside world—and why seeing Chinese people as individuals matters.  We talk about what it’s like to have your country, your culture, and your own identity be misunderstood.  We also talk about the growing desire among Chinese women to have more control over the lives they choose to live.  We talk about dating, marriage, motherhood, gender expectations and the fear of becoming “leftover”.  We explore how younger generations are challenging traditional norms and whether China’s changing social attitudes are pointing toward a more equal future.  We also talk about the loneliness of a world that feels increasingly divided, and Yaling’s hope that we can learn to see each other as individuals rather than stereotypes. It’s a conversation about identity, agency, belonging—and the fragile hope that we might find our way back to each other.

item.title: #191 Julie Sun: Love Practically
item.description:

item.title: #190- Eric Hovagim: The New American Dream
item.description:
Eric Hovagim is an American content producer, industrial engineer and political commentator who, in his own words, moved to China in late 2025 to escape "the American Century of Humiliation”.  He worked in New York City, producing a handful of videos that helped get Zohran Mamdani elected mayor in 2025.  Recently, Eric has been producing content for popular commentator, Hasan Piker.  He was previously also part of a climate-policy think tank in the US and an engineer on the Hyperloop team.  Today, we talk about why Eric is here in China and what he hopes to learn.  He shares his frustrations with the state of affairs in the US and the crisis of the American dream.  He argues the need for revolutionary change and optimism as we talk about what he’s observing in China that he could one day bring back to America.  We also talk about societal fear, AI concerns, Eric’s self-identification as a socialist and what annoys him about being here.  We share plenty of laughs in an otherwise serious discussion, and we might also have offended all French people.

item.title: #189- Raffe, BT & Dino: To Live and Die in Shanghai pt.2
item.description:

We talk about a renaissance in Shanghai’s dining scene, social media’s impact, and Cantina’s clientele flipping to 70% local Chinese. item.title: #186- Dr. Steve Vinay Gunther: The Truth About Us
item.description:
Dr. Steve Vinay Gunther is a renowned Australian Gestalt psychotherapist and founder of the acclaimed Northern Rivers Gestalt Institute in Australia.  He is also the author of the bestselling book “The Woman In Your Life - A Man’s Guide to a Happy Relationship”.  He has been in practice for over 40 years with an accomplished career in psychology, working with individuals, couples and families from all over the world.  

Today, Dr. Gunther shares why his focus shifted to China and we get into a deep conversation about relationships.  We talk about what prevents us from sustaining healthy relationships and when to walk away.  We cover failed marriages, self-awareness, listening for “grains of truth” and men’s difficulty identifying and expressing deeper feelings.   We talk about shame, “un-virtues” and why running away from pain doesn’t work.  We also discuss the over-simplification of therapy in this digital age, the dangers of using AI for emotional guidance, and a wholistic way of perceiving our own existence called systems thinking.  We explore relationships from at least three levels, the relationship with ourselves, the ones we love, and society.  Join us as we uncover some hard truths.

Dr. Brian Wong is a Rhodes Scholar, geopolitical strategist, tech advisor, author and Assistant Professor in Philosophy at the University of Hong Kong.  His research examines the intersection of geopolitics, political and moral philosophy, and technology.  Brian co-founded and now advises the Oxford Political Review and currently serves as a Fellow and Advisor at the Oxford Global Society, an independent think-tank.  He is also a Fellow at the Centre on Contemporary China and the World and is the Founding Secretary of Citizen Action Design, a youth policy think-tank based in Hong Kong.  Today we talk about the role of rhetoric and manufactured outrage in politics, the challenges of implementing true democracy, and the rise of AI.  We critique the notion of democracy as a panacea, and discuss a nuanced approach to governance in a multipolar world.  We dive into the current state of American politics, the factors contributing to the disillusionment and frustration among segments of the population, and cultural grievances weaponized by political elites.  We talk about AI and its potential impact on jobs and employment.  Brian expresses concern about the potential appointment of hawkish individuals in a Trump administration, exacerbating tensions and volatility in US-China relations.  He also expresses hope that the younger generations in both countries can help bridge divides.

item.description:

item.description:

item.title: #133. Gabor Holch: Beneath The Armor
item.description:
Gabor Holch is an intercultural leadership coach, speaker and author.  He has coached public leaders, CEO’s and high-level decision makers in some of the largest multinational companies in over 25 countries.  A former diplomat, he holds degrees in international relations, diplomacy and certifications in several assessment and coaching methodologies.  His latest book "Dragon Suit" is available now.  Today we discuss our human responses towards isolation, change, identity crises and technology.  We talk about its affect on our careers and personal life.  We talk about the power of confronting the very real question of "what is wrong with me?".  We get into the difficulties of adjusting back to normal life after an acute crisis, how it may strip you of self-confidence and how these changes result in a feeling of lost identity.  We talk about life's upward and downward curves, the "suit of armor" executives wear to hide their insecurities and when it might be good to show vulnerability at work and home. item.title: #132. Debora Malito: This Unstable World
item.description:
